jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

UC Berkeley’s Office of Strategic Communications leads communications for the No. 1 public university in the world. We tell the Berkeley story to inspire audiences and elevate the distinct narrative of the university's contributions to California and the world. Our mission is to promote the University’s excellence in education, discovery and public service. We provide leadership and services in five integrated functions: News and media relations, executive communications, internal communications, crisis communications, and marketing communications.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) serves as a communications advisor and speechwriter for the Chancellor of UC Berkeley. Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, this position is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive executive communications strategy that advances the Chancellor's leadership, supports other Cabinet leaders as needed, strengthens Berkeley’s institutional narrative, and fosters trust with internal and external constituencies.

The Executive Director brings a sophisticated understanding of how language, leadership, and strategy intersect – crafting communications that are precise, authentic, and aligned with the Chancellor's voice and the university's mission across every level of executive engagement, from day-to-day interactions to defining institutional moments.

The Executive Director also supervises and develops a small but growing team, currently including the Director of Executive Communications and the Director of Internal Communications, with additional direct reports anticipated as the function evolves. This role is a member of the Strategic Communications leadership team and plays a key part in building a cohesive and high-performing executive communications function within Strategic Communications.

In close partnership with the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, the Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) provides strategic communications counsel and executes a broad portfolio of executive communications on behalf of the Chancellor. This includes primary responsibility for all speechwriting, remarks, talking points, op-eds, social media, and all forms of communications supporting leadership engagement. This role also manages media relations specific to the Chancellor and other key leaders as needed, including triaging and responding to media requests, proactively developing Chancellor-centric visibility and profile opportunities, and advising on the reputational and communications dimensions of issues that directly involve the Chancellor.

The Executive Director develops and maintains a forward-looking executive communications plan that anticipates key moments, manages the Chancellor's speaking and engagement calendar from a communications perspective, and ensures consistency and strategic coherence across all Chancellor-facing communications. This position applies breadth and depth of higher education knowledge to navigate the complex organizational, political, and reputational landscape of a major public research university, and brings a contemporary understanding of how emerging technologies are reshaping executive communications and the stewardship of authentic leadership voice.

The Executive Director works in close coordination with the Chancellor's Office, Strategic Communications, and other senior leaders to ensure the Chancellor is well-prepared, well-positioned, and well-supported across all communications contexts.

This role also leads Berkeley’s internal communications function, developing and implementing a strategic approach to employee and campus community engagement that connects faculty and staff to the university’s mission, strategic priorities and leadership vision. This role also oversees Berkeley’s internal communications channels and editorial calendar, ensuring a regular and strategic cadence of communication that keeps the campus community informed, engaged, and connected to Berkeley’s broader institutional direction. The executive director is comfortable operating at both the strategic and executional level – bringing vision and structure while being willing to roll up their sleeves to get work done.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is: August 24, 2026 For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Develop and execute a comprehensive executive communications plan for the Chancellor that anticipates key moments, aligns with institutional priorities, and ensures strategic coherence across all communications contexts.
Support the Chancellor in the development of remarks, addresses, and presentations — serving as a skilled collaborator and writer who helps translate the Chancellor's own ideas, priorities, and voice into compelling communications for a wide range of audiences and occasions, from major institutional moments to day-to-day engagements
Draft talking points, op-eds, letters, messages to the campus community, video scripts, and other content that reflects the Chancellor's authentic voice and advances institutional priorities.
Manage the Chancellor's speaking and engagement calendar from a communications perspective, assessing, prioritizing, and developing opportunities for executive visibility.
Conduct research and interviews to inform content development, translating complex ideas and institutional priorities into clear, compelling language.

Proactively develop and pitch leadership visibility opportunities — including news stories, profiles, and thought leadership — that advance UC Berkeley's institutional priorities and reputation.
Manage media relations on behalf of the Chancellor and other executives as needed for institutional-level topics, issues, and priorities where the Chancellor serves as the primary voice and representative of UC Berkeley.
Triage and respond to media requests involving the Chancellor in coordination with the Media Relations office, senior leaders, and other subject matter experts, ensuring the Chancellor is well-prepared and strategically positioned on matters of institutional significance.
Prepare the Chancellor for media engagements by developing comprehensive briefing materials, anticipated questions, and key messages that reflect the full institutional context of the topics at hand.
Develop and maintain relationships with journalists and editors covering higher education, research, and issues of relevance to UC Berkeley and its mission.
Work with the Strategic Communications Issues team to monitor the media landscape for emerging opportunities and threats that may require the Chancellor's engagement as the institution's principal spokesperson.
Work with the Chancellor’s social media team on ensuring quality, engaging content that inspires and engages audiences.
Provide ongoing counsel on the reputational and communications dimensions of emerging issues and pending decisions that are likely to require the Chancellor's direct engagement.
Implement a strategic internal communications framework that connects faculty, staff, and students to the university's mission, priorities, and leadership vision - ensuring a regular and strategic cadence of communication that keeps the campus community informed and engaged.
Developing proactive and responsive strategies that help the campus community navigate complex, sensitive, and high-stakes moments – from institutional change to national events that reverberate on campus.
Serve as a strategic advisor to campus communicators across schools, colleges, and units - establishing best practices, developing shared frameworks and tools, and building a more coordinated approach to internal communications across the institution.
Provide supervision for the Executive Communications and Internal Communications team members, ensuring work is aligned with the Office of Strategic Communications' priorities. and supporting growth and development of the team..
Directly supervise employees by assigning work, establishing priorities, monitoring performance, and ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality communications.
Coach, mentor, and develop staff by establishing performance expectations, providing ongoing feedback, conducting performance evaluations, and supporting professional growth in accordance with university policies.

The Law School’s Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) team engages alumni philanthropically and in programming and initiatives that strengthen the school and the student experience. The mission of the Development arm is to secure financial support for core operations and special initiatives that advance the law school’s mission.

Position Overview

The position involves designing, developing, delivering, and administering fundraising programs. Develops and implements strategies for cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major gifts prospects with the capacity for a major gift of $25k to $1M and above; identifies new donor prospects through researching background information on potential donors and developing materials, creating marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; cultivates, stewards, and solicits donor prospects for gifts ranging from $25K to $1M and above; prepares and negotiates gift instruments ranging from moderate to high complexity; works with the Dean, Assistant Dean and faculty as necessary to solicit the largest gifts; manages a portfolio of principal gift prospects assigned to the Dean. Directs the research and preparation of the Dean’s briefings materials, creates talking points and meeting strategies for the Dean and briefs the Dean on these strategies. As appropriate, staffs the Dean on principal gifts visits and directs the tracking and implementation of all follow-up; manages the activities of the campaign cabinet and their meetings; collaborates with the Director of Financial Aid and the Director of Career Services to ensure proper stewardship of financial aid donors.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is: August 12, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Fundraising

Plans, organizes, and directs large-scale fundraising campaigns for Berkeley Law.
Participates in short- and long-range strategic planning. This includes annual stewardship for existing donors, long-term planning for prospect cultivation, foundation research and strategy, and campaign planning related to Berkeley Law endowment funds and long-term fundraising initiatives.
Identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards major gift prospects and donors, using established metrics (currently CADS) to track activity and report outcomes. Utilizes a return-on-investment approach in managing a donor portfolio.
Responsible for major gifts, corporate and foundation fundraising, and direct marketing efforts that generate philanthropic support for Berkeley Law. Manages a portfolio of donors with the capacity to give between $25,000 and $1,000,000 or more.
Writes complex proposals for individual, corporate, and foundation prospects.
Travels to meet with donors and represent Berkeley Law. Designs, organizes, and attends functions, meetings, and conferences as a representative of Berkeley Law. May serve on internal and external committees as a campus or Berkeley Law representative.
May participate in cross-campus, multi-unit fundraising campaigns in partnership with UDAR.
Ensures fundraising goals are achieved and raises at least $1 million annually by:
Managing a portfolio of 75–100 major gift and corporate/foundation prospects with the capacity to give $25,000–$1,000,000+.
Making 15–20 substantive donor contacts per month that advance relationships.
Conducting 80–120 donor visits annually.
Leading the planning and evaluation of fund development and annual solicitation programs, including financial feasibility studies, market research, and recommendations for program improvements.
Closing at least $1 million in new gift commitments or outright gifts.

Volunteer Engagement

May recruit, train, and support key volunteers who assist in advancement and fundraising efforts.

Program Leadership & Administration

May oversee the work of professional and support staff involved in implementing multi-component fundraising programs.
Uses key fundraising applications and databases to support fundraising strategies, goals, and objectives.

Professional Development & Other Duties

Engages in professional development and training opportunities as appropriate.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including relevant issues affecting the campus and higher education.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements, and organizational infrastructure.
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies related to gift acceptance, prospect management, and philanthropic fundraising.
Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the political acumen to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
Advanced skill in developing persuasive and compelling presentations that effectively communicate campus priorities and secure philanthropic support.
Advanced ability to achieve established goals and objectives through effective program and project planning, organization, execution, and evaluation.
Demonstrated commitment to and understanding of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB), with the ability to integrate DEIB principles into daily work and interactions.
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds represented within the UC Berkeley community.
Commitment to fostering an equitable, inclusive, and welcoming environment where students, faculty, staff, alumni, and donors of all backgrounds feel respected, supported, and valued.
Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to make sound decisions, identify and resolve complex issues, and develop creative solutions.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Advanced project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint, as well as UDAR fundraising systems and the ability to quickly learn new technologies.
Experience working with alumni, donors, volunteers, and other constituent groups, with the ability to cultivate and maintain positive, productive relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment.
Ability to travel and work evenings, approximately twice per month, as needed.
Demonstrated ability to meet or exceed fundraising goals and performance objectives.

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

Preferred Qualifications

Juris Doctor (JD) degree and/or experience in legal environments.
Membership in Council Advancement Secondary Education (CASE) and/or Association of Fundraising Professionals.

jobs.description:
Job Brief

Regional Deputy Director, Overdose Prevention Program

Vital Strategies is a global public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury, and death. We currently work in more than 80 countries, supporting data-driven decision-making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include noncommunicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, food policy, environmental health, and data for health. Our programs are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries and cities in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work.

We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by people with diverse life experiences whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or creed, gender, national origin, ancestry, actual or perceived age, physical or mental disability, veteran or military status, marital status, sexual orientation or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws. As such, our commitment is to promote equal employment opportunities (EEO) for those seeking employment.

About the Program:

The Overdose Prevention Program partners with U.S. states, Tribal Nations, and Native communities to advance evidence-based strategies that reduce overdose deaths. Through grant funding and tailored technical assistance, the program helps government, institutional, and community partners strengthen policies, implement innovative programs, and mobilize local action to address the evolving overdose crisis.

Our work spans the neighborhood, municipal, county, state, and Tribal levels, supporting sustainable public health solutions that are responsive to local needs. Program staff are organized into multidisciplinary regional teams, each managing a portfolio of states or Native communities. These teams work closely with colleagues in Operations and with subject matter experts in Communications, Program Evaluation & Knowledge Management, and Legal & Policy to deliver coordinated, high-impact support.

Job Purpose:

The Regional Deputy Director (RDD) leads strategy and program implementation for an assigned portfolio of states. Drawing on extensive experience working in state government working for an elected or senior agency official, the RDD spearheads the strategy and navigates the complexities of leading the government relations pillar of the program strategy. This role adapts overarching program goals, strategies, and directives to local contexts and is accountable for the strategic work plan, budget, and outcomes across the portfolio.

The RDD contributes their lived experience and professional knowledge while learning from the experience and expertise of colleagues as the team plans, monitors, and continually improves the program.

This is a new role for the Overdose Prevention program. It is a full-time position preferably based in the New York City metro area; we will consider other locations in the U.S. dependent on the work (North Carolina, New Jersey, Kentucky, New Mexico, Wisconsin, Nevada, or Washington state) . We offer highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position is $ 135,000 to $ 150,000 USD.

Functional Relationships:

Reporting to a Director, the RDD leads and supervises a multidisciplinary team of experts to integrate diverse perspectives into designing and managing effective programs across all facets of the program strategy. The position also collaborates closely with legal and policy and knowledge management.

The RDD serves as the senior point of contact with and provides expert guidance to state and local government partners in their region and liaises with key program partners. They will represent Vital Strategies at conferences with external stakeholders working on relevant overdose prevention.

To foster continuous learning, the RDD participates in an internal RDD Community of Practice and in key meetings with their peers and the program leadership team. While the Deputy’s work will focus primarily on their assigned region this role will also be required to share their expertise with and serve as a resource to other regions.

Duties and Responsibilities:

JOB DETAILS

Position Overview

The Executive Director is responsible for leading the entire community and supervising all community associates. This includes ensuring there is a positive and safe work environment in which residents are excited to live and team members are excited to work. This position reports to the Regional Vice President.

Key Business Areas

Morning Pointe has identified key business areas that will delineate the Executive Director areas of responsibility. Obviously, not all aspects of the position’s roles and responsibilities can be incorporated in this list.

Marketing And Community Relations

The ED is the sales leader for the community and will maintain target census level by creating a community sales culture and implementing external marketing plan.
Provide daily hands-on leadership in setting and executing sales goals and initiatives based on the company’s sales program; ensuring community meets sales Key Performance Indicators.
Participate in special events, marketing efforts and special programs, externally, as well as conducts tours to prospective families and residents.
Train all Directors and receptionists on conducting tours in the absence of the Executive Director or Community Relations Director.
Create, maintain, and ensure a positive environment throughout the community for residents, family, friends, and all team members, in alignment with the mission of Morning Pointe.
Promote positive image and build relationships to ensure favorable community relations.
Maintain current competitive analysis for utilization when developing budgets and to maintain competitive knowledge.
Participate in all new resident move-ins, including contract signing.

Financial Performance

Review at least monthly community revenue reporting, manage community budget and analyze financial statements, maintain budget accountability, anticipate and minimize negative budget variances and deficits; successfully manage operating expenses.
Accountable for meeting Net Operating Income (NOI) goals and budgeted revenue goals as defined by annual budget; review rent roll monthly at a minimum.
Implement monthly budgets for each department and ensure spend-downs are maintained.

General / Leadership

High moral and ethical values.
Responsibilities include supervision and quality control for all aspects of operations including marketing, staffing, resident care and services, budgeting, safety and building maintenance.
Ensure that the director team and associates maintain an environment which focuses on delivery of services by promoting individual resident capabilities through coordination of operations and programming functions for all departments.
Ensure that resident’s rights are well established and maintained at all times.
Ensure successful implementation of policies, procedures, and programs within the guidelines of state regulations and Morning Pointe policies.
Monitor resident, family, and associate satisfaction. Review complaints and grievances and makes written reports of action taken. Discuss such actions with appropriate parties.
Lead the community’s strategic planning initiative to establish goals and objectives in response to corporate goals.
Provide leadership, training and direction to the community leadership team and create annual development plans for each Director.
Inform supervisor and appropriate corporate office associates of any concerns related to the community, residents, or associates. Create reporting structure during absence of Executive Director.
Provide recognition and promote a positive and engaging culture for team members, residents, and families.
Strive to maintain a safe working environment through the prevention of accidents, the preservation of equipment, and the achievement of safe working practices.
Ensure that adequate supplies and equipment are on hand to meet the day-to-day operational needs of the community and residents.
With approval from management, responsible for securing annual Continuing Education Units required by the state to hold the appropriate administrator state license (if applicable) as a Morning Pointe Executive Director. Attend all required training, in-service, and staff meetings; participate in workshops, seminars, etc., to keep abreast of current data affecting senior living facilities, as well as to maintain a professional status.

Staff Management

Recruit, hire, retain, and coach high quality teams.
Ensure implementation of Morning Pointe staffing model and schedule labor hours consistent with staffing model (minimizing overtime) including proper level of staffing at all times.
Provide leadership and direction to all Directors and provide feedback concerning the operation of their departments to assist in eliminating/correcting problem areas, and/or improvement of services.
Lead staff meetings to ensure that appropriate information sharing is provided on a continuous basis.
Conduct operation meetings with Directors on a regular basis.
Maintain a cohesive team environment among departments.
Ensure appropriate new hire orientation and monthly in-service training for all associates is conducted while meeting state and corporate in-service training requirements.
Direct and evaluate management team during 90-day training period and annual review basis.
Approve and ensure that appropriate associate counseling and disciplinary actions occur.
Ensure that personnel files are created and maintained for all associates. Ensure record retention system meets state and corporate guidelines.
Review and approve bi-weekly payroll processing and ensure maintenance of appropriate documentation. Ensure record retention system meets state and corporate guidelines.
Ensure proper administration of Workers’ Compensation and Unemployment Compensation programs.
Participate and ensure required coverage for Manager on Duty program.
Establish proper reporting protocol is established in your absence.

Operations And Compliance

Assure compliance with local, state and federal regulations. Notify management of any visits by state officials. Give prompt attention to any cited deficiencies.
Support and successfully implement all Morning Pointe programs.
Approve all move-ins and move-outs.
Assist in preparing financial reports as requested.
Maintain records and investigate all incidents, accidents, or complaints.
Ensure maintenance of mandatory information, contracts, files, chemical specifications, and postings.
Review and approve all billing before forwarding to the Home Office.
Ensure maintenance of community Disaster Recovery Plan(s).
Ensure state regulations, company programs, policies and applicable guidelines are followed by associates, residents, visitors, and the general public.
Monitor resident care on a daily basis to ensure daily rounds and quality assurance programs are in place and enforced.
Establish and maintain a positive rapport with local and state agencies; ensure the community is survey ready at all times.

Resident Care

Responsible for ensuring specific programs, such as hydration, falls prevention, exercise and others as identified, are coordinated and implemented.
Ensure that Director of Nursing builds relationships and strong communication with residents and families to aid in the adjustment to Morning Pointe, identification of needs, concerns and appropriate service plan development for each resident.
Participate in care plan conferences as needed in coordination with Director of Nursing to review service plans with residents or families.
Ensure necessary ancillary services such as podiatry, dentistry, therapies, pharmacy consultation and similar services.

Resident Engagement

Ensure development of creative and exciting activity programming meeting Morning Pointe requirements with focuses on key aspects of healthy aging and individual preferences.
Conduct and/or arrange training to ensure all associates have an understanding of the purpose behind activity programming and special programs such as Morning Pointe in Motion, Meaningful Day, and Best Friends Approach.
Participate in activities calendar creation and ensure newsletters are distributed timely to newsletter database.

Dietary Services

Work collaboratively with Food Service Director to ensure dining services meets and/or improves targeted goals for food cost, food quality, and resident satisfaction.
Communicate resident dietary feedback to appropriate regional or corporate team members.

Asset Management

Ensure that the community, grounds, and property are maintained at the highest standard of excellence through preventative maintenance systems and programs. View the grounds and community through the eyes of a new visitor.
Routinely conduct community rounds with Maintenance Director.
Ensure work orders are completed timely to ensure a safe environment and satisfied customers.
Participate in interactive emergency drills. Ensure associates have a solid understanding of actions to be taken in emergency situation.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Demonstrated record of success in a leadership capacity.
Able to communicate effectively with all levels of associates, residents, family members, guests, vendors, referral sources, and the community at large.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; organizational and time management skills.
Intermediate level of computer and technology competency, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and other Microsoft Windows applications.
Passion for working with seniors.
Knowledge of customer service principles and practices.
Knowledge and understanding of the mission of Morning Pointe Senior Living.

Other Expectations

Perform other related essential duties as assigned.
Occasional travel is required and a valid driver’s license and proof of insurability is required.

Education And Experience Requirements

Bachelor's Degree in business administration, health care administration or other relevant course of study. Licensure required by state (if applicable).
Strong leadership skills with a minimum of two (2) years' experience in supervising and management.
A minimum of two (2) years' experience within a senior living environment or equivalent professional experience.
Required experience as an Executive Director in a healthcare setting

Physical Demands

Frequent lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, stooping, bending, turning, and stretching. Finger and hand dexterity required. Visual and hearing acuity essential. Ability to understand and carry out written and oral instructions necessary. Ability to perform basic mathematical computations required

Position Summary
We are looking for a passionate and self-directed team leader to develop, champion and execute the organization's fundraising strategy.  The Director of Development will build a diversified revenue base across individual giving, foundations, corporate partners, and government sources.  This person will report to the Executive Director and manage a two-person development team against clear monthly performance targets.

Duties and Responsibilities
Primary duties include: 
Strategy, Budget & Performance Management
Design and implement an annual development plan aligned to organizational goals and the operating budget
Own the development department budget, including expense management and ROI by channel
Set annual and monthly revenue goals, and track leading indicators — donor visits and meetings booked, qualification and solicitation counts, proposals submitted, ask amounts outstanding, pipeline value by stage, retention and upgrade rates
Report monthly on goals, pipeline, and variance to the ED; report quarterly to the board with analysis and course corrections
Major Gifts & Individual Giving
Manage a personal portfolio of mid-level & major donors and prospects through identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
Grow annual giving, monthly sustainers, and membership programs
Develop planned giving and legacy gift pathways
Institutional Funding
Oversee grant strategy, writing, submission, and reporting for foundation and government funders
Cultivate corporate sponsorships and cause-marketing partnerships
Team Leadership
Directly supervise two development staff; set individual goals, hold regular one-on-ones, and manage performance
Coach the team on moves management discipline and pipeline hygiene
Support and coach the ED and board members on their fundraising roles
Serve as a role model by adhering to and enforcing organizational policies, procedures and codes of conduct
Communications & Events
Partner on donor-facing communications, appeals, and impact reporting that translate conservation outcomes into compelling narratives
Lead fundraising events and donor engagement experiences, including site visits to conservation projects
Operations
Oversee the donor database, gift processing, acknowledgments, and data integrity
Ensure compliance with gift acceptance policies and grant reporting requirements

Required Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have a background and track record that includes: 
7–10 years of progressive nonprofit fundraising experience, including direct major gift solicitation
Demonstrated success closing five- and six-figure gifts
Experience supervising and developing staff
Track record of managing to metrics — comfort with budgets, forecasts, and leading-indicator dashboards
Grant writing and institutional funder management experience
Proficiency with CRM/donor databases and fundraising analytics
Excellent writing and interpersonal skills; comfort as a public face of the organization
Genuine interest in conservation, land stewardship, and environmental issues
Ability to work independently in a small-team environment where roles flex
Willingness to travel within California (primarily the SF Bay Area) and work occasional evenings/weekends.  Must have a valid California driver’s license or the ability to obtain one prior to employment.

Experience with river, watershed or land conservation organizations
CFRE certification

Proof of a valid California driver's license and insurance will be requested at the time of employment. 

Compensation & Benefits
This is a full time, exempt, remote position within the San Francisco Bay Area. Anticipated salary is $120,000 to $140,000 annually, including a generous benefits package (see below). Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications will be at or near the lower end of the compensation range. A candidate will land higher on the range according to the degree to which they exceed the minimum qualifications.  
Benefits: 
100% Employer paid medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage 
403(b) retirement plan with a 4% employer match 
2 weeks of paid vacation per year with an additional week each year of employment to a maximum of 4 weeks per year. 
14 paid holidays per year
3 personal days per year
12 days of paid sick leave per year 
Long term disability coverage 
Employer paid $10,000 life insurance policy 
For remote and/or hybrid work employees, monthly home office stipend for internet and cell service and one-time home office setup stipend 
3 weeks of Paid Parental Leave for employees with at least two years of employment

Work is primarily performed in an office environment (up to 60% of the time). Must be able to remain in a stationary position for extended periods (up to 8 hours per day), move items weighing up to 25 pounds, and move through the office and ascend/descend stairs. Frequent repetitive clerical tasks include but are not limited to operation of a computer keyboard, mouse, phone, tablet, and printer. Send an email with a resume and cover letter as pdf attachments with subject heading “Director of Development” to jobs@yosemiterivers.org .

If you have led a team:
 total dollars raised by the team annually, and year-over-year growth across your tenure. Please indicate amount raised by individuals, foundations, and government sources.

 you can attribute to your leadership

Yosemite Rivers Alliance is the voice for the rivers that define California’s Sierra heartland — the Tuolumne, Merced, and Stanislaus. Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

UC Berkeley’s Office of Strategic Communications leads communications for the No. 1 public university in the world. We tell the Berkeley story to inspire audiences and elevate the distinct narrative of the university's contributions to California and the world. Our mission is to promote the University’s excellence in education, discovery and public service. We provide leadership and services in five integrated functions: News and media relations, executive communications, internal communications, crisis communications, and marketing communications.

Position Summary

The Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) serves as a communications advisor and speechwriter for the Chancellor of UC Berkeley. Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, this position is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive executive communications strategy that advances the Chancellor's leadership, supports other Cabinet leaders as needed, strengthens Berkeley’s institutional narrative, and fosters trust with internal and external constituencies.

The Executive Director brings a sophisticated understanding of how language, leadership, and strategy intersect – crafting communications that are precise, authentic, and aligned with the Chancellor's voice and the university's mission across every level of executive engagement, from day-to-day interactions to defining institutional moments.

The Executive Director also supervises and develops a small but growing team, currently including the Director of Executive Communications and the Director of Internal Communications, with additional direct reports anticipated as the function evolves. This role is a member of the Strategic Communications leadership team and plays a key part in building a cohesive and high-performing executive communications function within Strategic Communications.

In close partnership with the Vice Chancellor for Strategic Communications, the Executive Director of Executive and Internal Communications (Executive Director) provides strategic communications counsel and executes a broad portfolio of executive communications on behalf of the Chancellor. This includes primary responsibility for all speechwriting, remarks, talking points, op-eds, social media, and all forms of communications supporting leadership engagement. This role also manages media relations specific to the Chancellor and other key leaders as needed, including triaging and responding to media requests, proactively developing Chancellor-centric visibility and profile opportunities, and advising on the reputational and communications dimensions of issues that directly involve the Chancellor.

The Executive Director develops and maintains a forward-looking executive communications plan that anticipates key moments, manages the Chancellor's speaking and engagement calendar from a communications perspective, and ensures consistency and strategic coherence across all Chancellor-facing communications. This position applies breadth and depth of higher education knowledge to navigate the complex organizational, political, and reputational landscape of a major public research university, and brings a contemporary understanding of how emerging technologies are reshaping executive communications and the stewardship of authentic leadership voice.

The Executive Director works in close coordination with the Chancellor's Office, Strategic Communications, and other senior leaders to ensure the Chancellor is well-prepared, well-positioned, and well-supported across all communications contexts.

This role also leads Berkeley’s internal communications function, developing and implementing a strategic approach to employee and campus community engagement that connects faculty and staff to the university’s mission, strategic priorities and leadership vision. This role also oversees Berkeley’s internal communications channels and editorial calendar, ensuring a regular and strategic cadence of communication that keeps the campus community informed, engaged, and connected to Berkeley’s broader institutional direction. The executive director is comfortable operating at both the strategic and executional level – bringing vision and structure while being willing to roll up their sleeves to get work done.

Develop and execute a comprehensive executive communications plan for the Chancellor that anticipates key moments, aligns with institutional priorities, and ensures strategic coherence across all communications contexts.
Support the Chancellor in the development of remarks, addresses, and presentations — serving as a skilled collaborator and writer who helps translate the Chancellor's own ideas, priorities, and voice into compelling communications for a wide range of audiences and occasions, from major institutional moments to day-to-day engagements

Coordinate with the Office of the Chancellor, Strategic Communications, and other subject matter experts to ensure the Chancellor is well-prepared and well-positioned across all communications contexts.
Apply emerging tools and technologies to the communications development process in ways that enhance the communications process and outcomes.
Proactively develop and pitch leadership visibility opportunities — including news stories, profiles, and thought leadership — that advance UC Berkeley's institutional priorities and reputation.
Manage media relations on behalf of the Chancellor and other executives as needed for institutional-level topics, issues, and priorities where the Chancellor serves as the primary voice and representative of UC Berkeley.

Managing a portfolio of 75–100 major gift and corporate/foundation prospects with the capacity to give $25,000–$1,000,000+.

Conducting 80–120 donor visits annually.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Regional Deputy Director, Overdose Prevention Program

Vital Strategies is a global public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury, and death. We currently work in more than 80 countries, supporting data-driven decision-making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include noncommunicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, food policy, environmental health, and data for health. Our programs are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries and cities in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work.

We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by people with diverse life experiences whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or creed, gender, national origin, ancestry, actual or perceived age, physical or mental disability, veteran or military status, marital status, sexual orientation or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal laws. As such, our commitment is to promote equal employment opportunities (EEO) for those seeking employment.

About the Program:

The Overdose Prevention Program partners with U.S. states, Tribal Nations, and Native communities to advance evidence-based strategies that reduce overdose deaths. Through grant funding and tailored technical assistance, the program helps government, institutional, and community partners strengthen policies, implement innovative programs, and mobilize local action to address the evolving overdose crisis.

Our work spans the neighborhood, municipal, county, state, and Tribal levels, supporting sustainable public health solutions that are responsive to local needs. Program staff are organized into multidisciplinary regional teams, each managing a portfolio of states or Native communities. These teams work closely with colleagues in Operations and with subject matter experts in Communications, Program Evaluation & Knowledge Management, and Legal & Policy to deliver coordinated, high-impact support.

Job Purpose:

The Regional Deputy Director (RDD) leads strategy and program implementation for an assigned portfolio of states. Drawing on extensive experience working in state government working for an elected or senior agency official, the RDD spearheads the strategy and navigates the complexities of leading the government relations pillar of the program strategy. This role adapts overarching program goals, strategies, and directives to local contexts and is accountable for the strategic work plan, budget, and outcomes across the portfolio.

The RDD contributes their lived experience and professional knowledge while learning from the experience and expertise of colleagues as the team plans, monitors, and continually improves the program.

This is a new role for the Overdose Prevention program. It is a full-time position preferably based in the New York City metro area; we will consider other locations in the U.S. dependent on the work (North Carolina, New Jersey, Kentucky, New Mexico, Wisconsin, Nevada, or Washington state) . We offer highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position is $ 135,000 to $ 150,000 USD.

Functional Relationships:

Reporting to a Director, the RDD leads and supervises a multidisciplinary team of experts to integrate diverse perspectives into designing and managing effective programs across all facets of the program strategy. The position also collaborates closely with legal and policy and knowledge management.

The RDD serves as the senior point of contact with and provides expert guidance to state and local government partners in their region and liaises with key program partners. They will represent Vital Strategies at conferences with external stakeholders working on relevant overdose prevention.

While the Deputy’s work will focus primarily on their assigned region this role will also be required to share their expertise with and serve as a resource to other regions.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Collective Planning and State Strategy Development -

Lead a regional multidisciplinary team and contribute unique perspective to develop and monitor implementation of a comprehensive state strategy, annual work plan and budget that integrates the collective expertise of the team, current overdose data and epidemiology, state policy landscapes, community needs, and lessons learned from prior implementation with inclusion of support from Principal and Senior Technical Advisors and OPP Directors.
Collaborate with the other regions and team members to review all proposed plans and ensure priorities align with programmatic goals.
Cultivate a culture of curiosity and shared learning that supports a holistic approach to programming: consult regularly with colleagues on needs related to core responsibilities and expertise; and adapt own planning to integrate other professional perspectives.
Apply an intersectional racial justice framework across all planning processes, program design, and implementation.

Program Management and Leadership -

Manage regional budget, monitor budget vs. actuals ensuring expenditures are in line with work plans. Lead the ongoing management of approved work plans and associated budgets; with support from Operations, monitor budget-versus-actuals on a regular basis and adjust activities as needed.
Lead the team to continually monitor progress of each work plan through robust metrics, quality improvement (QI) frameworks, and MERLA (Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, Learning, and Adaptation) processes.
Oversee the design, negotiation, and implementation of sub-grants to state and local governments, providers, coalitions, and community organizations, in accordance with established policies and processes by Vital’s Grants and Contracts department.
Support the regional team in developing strategic investment proposals for new partnerships and funding opportunities with community-based and institutional providers and system actors, (including substance use treatment, harm reduction services, criminal justice corrections and supervision, emergency medical services, child and family welfare, healthcare, and housing services) and present to OPP leadership for approval.
Identify and prioritize opportunities for legal, policy analysis, and litigation strategy in partnership with legal/policy team; oversee implementation within the portfolio.
Identify and prioritize needs and opportunities within the regional portfolio with the team and develop action plans for implementation as appropriate.
Partner with the Knowledge Management Lead to design and apply a regional learning strategy that captures and disseminates implementation insights.

Strategic State and Local Government Engagement and Technical Assistance

Serve as the primary representative and senior point of contact for state and local government partners across the assigned portfolio.
Using prior work experience in a city or state government to help successfully navigate the structure, build and maintain trusted working relationships with elected officials, policy makers, state agencies, and local government leadership.
Identify and develop government-embedded positions (via MOUs or similar mechanisms) to advance strategic program priorities within agencies, in collaboration with regional team staff and government partners with approval from OPP Leadership.
Represent the program at stakeholder meetings and deliver presentations to government, provider, and community audiences.
Serve as a senior technical resource to government partners on overdose prevention interventions, setting-specific strategies, and financing options, including for naloxone distribution, low-barrier treatment, harm reduction services, and recovery supports.
Oversee the design, management, and delivery of technical assessments, training, and capacity-building support to state and local partners and sub-grantees.
Maintain current expertise on scientific, policy, and practice developments in overdose prevention, and routinely assess jurisdictional applicability of emerging interventions.

Team Leadership & Development -

Lead by modeling Vital Strategies’ core values: respect, inclusive collaboration, ability to adapt and continuous learning.
Foster a high-performing, collaborative team culture rooted in accountability, transparency, and inclusive decision-making,
Supervise, support, and guide a diverse team of technical professionals to develop, implement and monitor strategic work plans.
Manage staff for technical and programmatic work, mentor staff for career development, and support staff to promote professional growth.
Ensure regional team members participate in their respective Communities of Practice.
Foster open communication and a spirit of teamwork across the regional team as well as with other teams and colleagues.

Cross-Cutting Collaboration & Coordination -

Collaborate with Bloomberg Overdose Prevention Initiative partners on strategic prioritization and joint implementation.
Support communications needs, as appropriate, and contribute to ad hoc organizational priorities as assigned.

Education -

Bachelor's degree in public health, public policy, nursing, social work, healthcare administration, or a related field required, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Advanced degree (MPH, MSW, MHA, JD, MD, or equivalent) preferred.

Skills & Abilities -

Demonstrated subject matter expertise in harm reduction, overdose prevention, and drug policy, developed through direct service and programmatic leadership at the community, local, or regional level.
Understanding of legislative and regulatory frameworks relevant to harm reduction and public health interventions, including the ability to advise partners on policy implementation.

Position Summary
We are looking for a passionate and self-directed team leader to develop, champion and execute the organization's fundraising strategy.  The Director of Development will build a diversified revenue base across individual giving, foundations, corporate partners, and government sources.  This person will report to the Executive Director and manage a two-person development team against clear monthly performance targets.

Primary duties include: 
Strategy, Budget & Performance Management
Design and implement an annual development plan aligned to organizational goals and the operating budget
Own the development department budget, including expense management and ROI by channel
Set annual and monthly revenue goals, and track leading indicators — donor visits and meetings booked, qualification and solicitation counts, proposals submitted, ask amounts outstanding, pipeline value by stage, retention and upgrade rates
Report monthly on goals, pipeline, and variance to the ED; report quarterly to the board with analysis and course corrections
Major Gifts & Individual Giving
Manage a personal portfolio of mid-level & major donors and prospects through identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
Grow annual giving, monthly sustainers, and membership programs
Develop planned giving and legacy gift pathways
Institutional Funding
Oversee grant strategy, writing, submission, and reporting for foundation and government funders
Cultivate corporate sponsorships and cause-marketing partnerships
Team Leadership
Directly supervise two development staff; set individual goals, hold regular one-on-ones, and manage performance
Coach the team on moves management discipline and pipeline hygiene
Support and coach the ED and board members on their fundraising roles
Serve as a role model by adhering to and enforcing organizational policies, procedures and codes of conduct
Communications & Events
Partner on donor-facing communications, appeals, and impact reporting that translate conservation outcomes into compelling narratives
Lead fundraising events and donor engagement experiences, including site visits to conservation projects
Operations
Oversee the donor database, gift processing, acknowledgments, and data integrity
Ensure compliance with gift acceptance policies and grant reporting requirements

Required Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have a background and track record that includes: 
7–10 years of progressive nonprofit fundraising experience, including direct major gift solicitation
Demonstrated success closing five- and six-figure gifts
Experience supervising and developing staff
Track record of managing to metrics — comfort with budgets, forecasts, and leading-indicator dashboards
Grant writing and institutional funder management experience
Proficiency with CRM/donor databases and fundraising analytics
Excellent writing and interpersonal skills; comfort as a public face of the organization
Genuine interest in conservation, land stewardship, and environmental issues
Ability to work independently in a small-team environment where roles flex
Willingness to travel within California (primarily the SF Bay Area) and work occasional evenings/weekends.  Must have a valid California driver’s license or the ability to obtain one prior to employment. 

Preferred Qualifications
Preferred qualifications include:
Experience with river, watershed or land conservation organizations
CFRE certification
Remote position with a location within the San Francisco Bay Area

Travel This position will be primarily remote office-based (60%) with frequent travel required (40%) to donor engagements across the Bay Area and occasionally to our offices in Modesto and Sonora.  Occasional overnight travel may be needed for donor meetings and special events in more distant locations. Proof of a valid California driver's license and insurance will be requested at the time of employment. 

Compensation & Benefits
This is a full time, exempt, remote position within the San Francisco Bay Area. Anticipated salary is $120,000 to $140,000 annually, including a generous benefits package (see below). Candidates who meet the minimum qualifications will be at or near the lower end of the compensation range. A candidate will land higher on the range according to the degree to which they exceed the minimum qualifications.  
Benefits: 
100% Employer paid medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage 
403(b) retirement plan with a 4% employer match 
2 weeks of paid vacation per year with an additional week each year of employment to a maximum of 4 weeks per year. 
14 paid holidays per year
3 personal days per year
12 days of paid sick leave per year 
Long term disability coverage 
Employer paid $10,000 life insurance policy 
For remote and/or hybrid work employees, monthly home office stipend for internet and cell service and one-time home office setup stipend 
3 weeks of Paid Parental Leave for employees with at least two years of employment 

Essential Job Functions
Work is primarily performed in an office environment (up to 60% of the time). Must be able to remain in a stationary position for extended periods (up to 8 hours per day), move items weighing up to 25 pounds, and move through the office and ascend/descend stairs. Frequent repetitive clerical tasks include but are not limited to operation of a computer keyboard, mouse, phone, tablet, and printer. Occasionally (up to 40% of the time) spends up to 6 hours per day in a vehicle. May be required to work evenings and/or weekends.

To Apply
Send an email with a resume and cover letter as pdf attachments with subject heading “Director of Development” to jobs@yosemiterivers.org . 

Please include:
If you have led a team:
 total dollars raised by the team annually, and year-over-year growth across your tenure. Please indicate amount raised by individuals, foundations, and government sources.
If you have not led a team:
 the size and composition of your personal portfolio of individual donors, dollars raised annually, and year-over-year growth
Donor retention rates
 and how they trended under your management
Year-over-year revenue growth
 you can attribute to your leadership
Size of teams and budgets
 you have managed

Applications without documented results will not be considered.

This position will remain open until filled, but priority will be given to applications received by August 28th.

Yosemite Rivers Alliance is the voice for the rivers that define California’s Sierra heartland — the Tuolumne, Merced, and Stanislaus. We promote stewardship of these rivers and their tributaries to ensure healthy watersheds, from the peaks of Yosemite National Park to the San Francisco Bay. We are the only organization working throughout all three watersheds, linking Sierra and Central Valley conservation issues and forging strong ties between rural mountain communities and Bay Area urban centers.

In 2025, we expanded our mission and became Yosemite Rivers Alliance — carrying forward a proven legacy while stepping into a broader responsibility to protect the interconnected rivers that sustain millions of people and countless species across the region.

new_jobs.description:
Alliance for American Leadership (A4AL)

About the Organization

The Alliance for American Leadership is a bipartisan coalition working to revitalize U.S. global leadership through strategic investments in international development. We believe foreign aid is one of the most cost-effective tools in policymakers' arsenal. It is less than one percent of the federal budget, yet it fights global poverty, strengthens U.S. national security, prevents pandemics, and bolsters the U.S. economy. Further, a study in the Lancet projects that 14 million people may die over the next four years if foreign aid is not restored. To prevent that, A4AL drafts policy, lobbies Congress, runs digital ad campaigns that reach millions of Americans, and supports the campaigns of Members of Congress who defend foreign aid.
Position Overview:
The Fundraising Director leads the Alliance's overall fundraising strategy and operations. The role owns annual fundraising planning, the calendar of fundraising events, the donor pipeline as a whole, and coalition fundraising with partner organizations. The Fundraising Director partners with the Director of Major Gifts on the largest donor relationships and supervises the Development Operations Manager who runs the day-to-day systems. Reports to the Executive Director (or Managing Director, when filled). This is a remote, unpaid volunteer role and one of the highest-leverage senior positions in the Alliance.

Core Responsibilities

Fundraising Strategy

Develop and execute the Alliance's annual fundraising plan, including revenue targets, donor segments, and the calendar of campaigns and events.
Set strategy for grassroots fundraising, mid-level donors, major gifts (in partnership with the Director of Major Gifts), and institutional funders.
Identify the highest-leverage windows for fundraising pushes — particularly the post-election January-to-June window — and concentrate effort there.

Donor Pipeline & Cultivation

Own the donor pipeline as a whole — tracking prospects from first touch through cultivation, ask, and stewardship.
Coordinate with the Director of Major Gifts on the cultivation of five and six-figure donor relationships.
Coordinate with the Endorsements Committees on donor relationships that overlap with the bipartisan endorsement program.

Events & Campaigns

Lead the planning and execution of fundraising events, in partnership with the Director of Virtual Events.
Drive grassroots fundraising campaigns including monthly giving, end-of-year appeals, and rapid-response fundraising tied to news moments.
Track event-by-event and campaign-by-campaign performance and refine based on what works.

Team Leadership

Manage the Deputy Fundraising Directors and the Development Operations Manager.
Mentor junior fundraising staff and volunteers, building the Alliance's internal fundraising capacity over time.
Coordinate with the Communications team on fundraising messaging, donor-facing content, and public campaigns.

Qualifications

Significant experience in nonprofit or political fundraising, including direct ownership of fundraising strategy and execution.
Track record of meeting fundraising targets across multiple donor segments.
Strong donor-facing presence — comfortable in cultivation conversations with sophisticated donors.
Operational discipline and the ability to manage a multi-channel fundraising operation.
Existing relationships in the foreign assistance, international development, or political donor community preferred.
Commitment to A4AL's bipartisan mission and values.

Job Summary

The Managing Director, Generation Plant Engineering, is responsible for working with I&M Generation Leadership and plant operations teams to provide technical direction and oversight of all plant level engineering matters across the company’s generation fleet. This role works closely with AEP’s central engineering organization to ensure all AEP engineering standards, design basis, best practices, and technical requirements are implemented at I&M’s generation sites. This position also works closely with plant operations to provide training and oversight to operations staff, engage in troubleshooting operational issues, lead root cause analysis, and coordinate third party technical support. This leadership position also emphasizes continuous improvement, regulatory compliance, and the integration of new technologies to enhance performance and efficiency across all generation assets.

Job Description

What You'll Do:

Strategic Leadership

Actively participate on I&M Generation Leadership team in the development and implementation of the technical vision and strategic direction for the generation organization.
Serve as I&M’s primary lead for communication and coordination with AEP’s central engineering team on technical strategic plan and new technologies.
Establish long-term strategies along with near-term goals, action plans, and performance objectives.

Engineering Oversight

Direct and oversee plant level engineering activities across I&M’s generation facilities.
Provide timely engineering and technical support to Plant Managers and coordinate activities with AEP central engineering and/or third-party technical support as necessary.
Actively engage with operations teams and engineering support to ensure alignment with project schedules, budgets, and resource plans.

Standards & Compliance

Ensure operations staff at each I&M facility is property trained and operates I&M generation facilities in accordance with engineering design standards and guidelines consistent with industry regulations and company requirements.
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local safety and environmental regulations.

Technology & Innovation

Work with AEP central engineering and I&M Generation Leadership to evaluate, select, and implement new technologies, equipment, and vendor solutions to improve performance and reduce cost.
Drive modernization and digital transformation initiatives within I&M’s generation portfolio.

Planning & Budgeting

Work with Plant Managers in the development of annual work plans, capital projects, and resource forecasts.
Lead the development and coordination of Asset Health Reports for I&M generation assets and develop long-term investment plans to support safe and reliable operations.

Operational Excellence

Work with I&M Generation Leadership team and Plant Managers to promote and enforce robust safety, health, and environmental programs at I&M Generation facilities.
Work with Plant Managers to ensure strong quality control processes and continuous improvement practices are in place.

Talent Management

Participate in recruiting, developing, and retaining a high-performing plant engineering workforce.
Develop and implement training programs that increase the engineering and technical skills of I&M’s workforce,

Contractor & Vendor Management

Work with AEP central engineering and procurement to ensure proper technical specifications, scopes of work, and quality control processes are in place for contractors and vendors performing work on I&M generation facilities.
Ensure accountability, cost effectiveness, and service quality of all third-party engineering and technical firms used to perform work on I&M generation assets.

What We're Looking For:

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field(Master’s degree preferred).
Professional Engineer (PE) license or equivalent certification is preferred

Experience:

Minimum of 12 years of progressive engineering experience within power generation.
At least 4 years of leadership or management experience.

Key Competencies

Strategic and business leadership
Technical expertise in generation systems (e.g., fossil, renewables, or multi-technology fleets)
Financial and operational acumen
Change leadership and innovation mindset
Talent development and team leadership
Cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement

Work Environment

Office-based with travel up to 25% to generation facilities.
Involves work in industrial environments, including exposure to standard plant conditions.

Where You'll Work:

On-Site in Indianapolis, IN, Fort Wayne, IN or Rockport, IN

Long-term incentive
401K match
